source.title: Constructed exercise (not from a publication): a water pump from 1 atm to 5 bar
source.note: every input is my choice, flagged assumed. The topic comes from the IIT Kharagpur NPTEL course plan (Principles and Practices of Process Equipment and Plant Design, week 10: plant hydraulics, pumps and compressors); the lectures are videos and their transcripts could not be reached, so none of their content or numbers is used

reported.name: pump_duty
reported.anchor: independent: CoolProp IAPWS-95, isentropic enthalpy rise 0.5331 kJ/kg divided by an efficiency of 0.75 (DWSIM's default, to be confirmed by the run), x 36000 kg/h

reported.name: outlet_T
reported.anchor: independent: outlet enthalpy at the outlet pressure, same efficiency

tolerance.note: duty 2 percent and outlet temperature 1 percent (of the value in C), fixed before the run; the efficiency of 0.75 is DWSIM's default, which I have not confirmed before this run

scenarios.why: the same pump to 20 bar: the duty scales with the pressure rise (independent calculation)
twice the flow: the duty doubles, the outlet temperature does not change (independent calculation)

review.method: independent isentropic and isenthalpic calculations with CoolProp
